title: Product PRD & Roadmap: Unified Inference — Overview, Requirements, Design, Pricing, Release Notes
author: Ava Thompson
body:
Summary:
This document consolidates the product overview, PRD highlights, high-level requirements, design specifications, roadmap themes, pricing & packaging guidance, and release notes for the Unified Inference product family (Hosted API, Dedicated, Private) for FY26–FY27. Intended readers: product managers, engineering leads, solutions engineering, sales, and customer success.

1) Product overview
Purpose:
- Provide a single, consistent runtime and developer experience for LLM inference across Hosted, Dedicated and Private deployments.
Key capabilities:
- Text generation, chat, embeddings, reranking, and tool/function calling.
- Model catalog with versioning, rollout policies, and verified performance profiles.
- Cost/performance controls: batching, caching, quantization profiles, routing policies.
- Observability: per-model and per-route dashboards, token-level cost breakdown, traces.
- Deployment modes: Hosted API (self-serve), Dedicated (reserved GPU pools), Private (VPC/on-prem).
Primary personas:
- Software engineers embedding LLMs into products.
- ML engineers responsible for production inference.
- Platform teams standardizing model serving across business units.

2) Product goals and success metrics
Goals (12–18 months):
- Deliver single API surface across deployment modes with <100ms median token latency for common text workloads (up to 512 tokens).
- Reduce per-token cost for high-throughput customers by 20% via improved batching and caching suggestions.
- Increase self-serve conversion to Dedicated engagements by 15% via new sizing and onboarding flows.
- Provide regression detection workflows (prompt-set based) and integrate with Redwood Optimize.
KPIs / success metrics:
- Latency P50/P95 for Hosted API (target: P50 <80ms, P95 <220ms for 512-token workloads).
- Unit cost per 1K tokens (tracked by model and quantization profile).
- Adoption: monthly active API keys, Dedicated contract conversions, Private deployment wins.
- Reliability: SLO compliance (request success >99.9%), error budget burn.

3) PRD summary and requirements
Scope (in-scope):
- Unified inference API parity across Hosted, Dedicated, Private.
- Model versioning and rollout (canary, A/B, automatic fallback).
- Cost/perf controls surfaced in Console and via API (batch_size, cache_ttl, quantization_profile).
- Observability: token-level cost, per-route latency histogram, prompt-set regression alerts.
Out of scope (for this release):
- New on-prem packaging format (next release cycle).
- Custom hardware procurement marketplace.

Functional requirements (high-level):
- FR-01: API must accept a standardized request that supports streaming, function/tool call hints, and structured output schema fields.
- FR-02: Users must be able to pin model version and configure rollout policy per route.
- FR-03: Console must provide suggested batching and caching profiles derived from traffic analysis.
- FR-04: System must support automatic fallback to compatible model variants when capacity constrained.

Non-functional requirements (NFRs):
- NFR-01: Latency targets documented above.
- NFR-02: Availability SLOs: Hosted API 99.9% monthly; Dedicated per-contract SLA.
- NFR-03: Security: all customer data encrypted in transit and at rest; Private deployments must integrate with customer KMS.
- NFR-04: Scalability: support 5x peak traffic observed during load tests without manual intervention.
- NFR-05: Observability retention: token-level metrics retained 90 days (configurable for enterprise).

Acceptance criteria (examples):
- AC-01: End-to-end latency measured in production meets P95 targets for 90% of test routes under realistic load.
- AC-02: Console shows persistent suggested batching profile with expected cost savings >10% in pilot customers.
- AC-03: Rollout policy changes can be executed and rolled back via Console within 5 minutes.

4) Design specifications
High-level architecture:
- Control plane: centralized config and rollout APIs, metadata store (per-customer routing and model pins).
- Serving plane: runtime clusters (GPU-attached) with kernel selection layer and batching coordinator.
- Observability pipeline: trace collector, token-metering service, metrics store (Prometheus + long-term TSDB).

APIs and contract:
- Request contract (example fields): model, model_version, route_id, prompt, max_tokens, temperature, streaming=true|false, tools=[...], output_schema.
- Rollout API: create_rollout(route_id, model_version, policy={canary_percent, step_duration}, fallback_models=[]).
- Billing contract: per-token counters emitted by token-metering service and reconciled daily with billing.

Design tradeoffs considered:
- Centralized vs federated config: centralized simplifies rollouts/analytics but requires robust control-plane HA and caching. We choose centralized control plane with read-through caches in serving clusters to meet low-latency requirements.
- Strong consistency for rollout decisions vs eventual: we use near-real-time propagation (sub-second for critical flags) with graceful fallback to pinned model version if propagation fails.

Operational concerns and runbook highlights:
- Deploy strategy: canary-by-cluster then canary-by-route.
- Rollback: immediate rollback via control-plane flag; serving cluster will drain and resume pinned model.
- Monitoring: alert on token-metering mismatch >0.5% and rollout success <99%.

Security and compliance:
- Private deployments: KMS integration for model artifacts and customer data; audit log per request.
- Data minimization: configurable logging levels for PII-sensitive routes.

5) Roadmap & themes (next 4 quarters)
Q3 2026 (now–Sep 2026):
- Launch v1 unified API parity for Hosted; basic rollout and model pinning; per-route dashboards.
- Pilot Dedicated onboarding workflow and SLO monitoring.
Q4 2026 (Oct–Dec 2026):
- Console suggestions for batching/caching; basic quantization recommendation engine.
- Release unified rollout API with canary/A-B and automatic fallback.
Q1 2027 (Jan–Mar 2027):
- Private deployment pilot (VPC) with KMS/HSM integration and extended observability retention.
- Billing reconciliation automation and partner marketplace listing.
Q2 2027 (Apr–Jun 2027):
- Expanded Optimize recommendations (model selection + quant profiles per workload).
- SLA enhancements and self-serve Dedicated sizing engine.
Cross-cutting themes:
- Production economics: every feature should include expected unit-cost impact.
- Developer experience: reduce time-to-first-success (TTFS) and improve docs/quickstarts.
- Reliability-first rollouts: safe defaults and automatic fallbacks.

6) Pricing & packaging notes
Guiding principles:
- Pricing should reflect unit economics and provide predictable options for scale customers.
- Offer entry-level Hosted pricing to enable PLG adoption; provide committed discounts for Dedicated.
Packaging tiers (examples):
- Developer (Hosted): pay-as-you-go, per-token pricing, limited SLA (best-effort), free-tier credits.
- Business (Hosted + Dedicated trial): volume discounts, per-route quotas, 99.9% uptime SLO for critical routes.
- Enterprise (Dedicated + Private): committed reserved capacity pricing; optional platform fee; premium SLAs and long-term retention.
Representative pricing table (illustrative):
- Developer: $0.0018 per 1K input tokens; $0.0042 per 1K output tokens; embeddings $0.0006 per vector.
- Business: 20% off list at 100M tokens/month commit; Dedicated starts at $12k/month per GPU pool with burst credits.
- Enterprise: Custom pricing; platform fee $2k–$10k/month depending on features and retention.
Discount & commitment notes:
- Commitments evaluated quarterly; rollover credits allowed up to 10% of committed volume.
- Early-adopter pricing pilots for Dedicated customers in Q4 2026 to collect usage and sizing feedback.

7) Release notes (recent release: Unified Inference v1.3 — 2026-11-30)
Release highlights:
- GA: Unified API parity for text generation and embeddings across Hosted and Dedicated.
- Rollouts: Canary and A/B rollout policies available via Console and API.
- Observability: token-level cost breakdown and per-route latency histograms.
- Console: batching/caching suggestions appear in route recommendations.

Notable bug fixes:
- Fixed kernel selection regression that increased P95 by 12% under certain seq-len patterns (fix: prioritized short-seq kernels).
- Resolved token-metering mismatch in presence of streaming responses.

Known issues and mitigations:
- Issue: Quantization suggestions occasionally propose unsupported profile for older model variants. Mitigation: Console flags unsupported profiles and prevents selection.
- Issue: Initial Dedicated onboarding has manual sizing steps for certain multi-tenant configs. Mitigation: solutions engineering playbook and expedited onboarding support.

Rollout plan and ownership:
- Release window: 2026-11-30 to 2026-12-07 staged rollout.
- Owners: Product: Ava Thompson; Eng-SRE: Diego Martinez; Eng-Serving-Runtime: Priya Rao; Solutions Eng: Kunal Mehta.
- Rollback criteria: >1% customer-facing error rate increase or >25% SLA violations for key routes within 2 hours.

8) Implementation checklist (milestones before GA)
- Complete API contract and SDK updates.
- Finish rollout API implementation and end-to-end e2e tests.
- Console UX for batching/caching suggestions and rollout controls.
- Observability pipeline validation and billing reconciliation tests.
- Customer pilot with at least two Dedicated customers and one Private evaluation.

9) Open decisions and risks
Open decisions:
- Pricing floor for high-frequency inference customers (final decision due 2026-12-15).
- Retention windows for token-level metrics for Business tier customers (awaiting finance input).
Risks:
- Model performance regressions when using aggressive quantization; mitigation: A/B with quality guardrails and eval prompt-sets.
- Control plane scale under cross-customer rollout churn; mitigation: read-through caches and rate-limited rollout changes.

10) Appendix: quick reference commands and examples
- Rollout API example:
  curl -X POST https://api.redwood.ai/v1/rollouts -H "Authorization: Bearer $TOKEN" -d '{"route_id":"chat-bot","model_version":"redwood-2.1.0","policy":{"canary_percent":10,"step_duration":"30m"},"fallback_models":["redwood-2.0.3"]}'

- Suggested observability thresholds:
  - Alert if route P95 > 1.5x baseline for 10 minutes.
  - Alert if token-metering mismatch > 0.5% for 5 minutes.
